suite.name: math-worksheets end-to-end capability suite
suite.purpose: Evaluate whether an agent using the math-worksheets skill produces correct, requested, printable worksheet artifacts and respects the skill's trust boundaries.

hard_gates: Exactly one readable worksheet PDF, one readable step-by-step answer-key PDF, and one readable 1-2 page skills-summary PDF are produced and surfaced to the user.
The worksheet contains the requested number of student problems; examples and try-it boxes in the skills summary do not count as worksheet problems.
The worksheet and skills-summary verification JSON files exist, parse, cover every printed item, and pass the repository gate chain with exit 0.
An independently authored math oracle finds zero incorrect final answers and zero statement/answer mismatches.
No severe clipping, overlap, blank-page, unreadable-font, missing-glyph, or zero-workspace defect appears in rendered PDFs.
Every explicit user requirement and every task-specific assertion is satisfied.
quality_dimensions: concise delivery message with working artifact paths or attachments

hard_gate_overrides: Exit 2/manual-review is acceptable and expected for genuinely open items; it must be disclosed rather than described as machine-verified.
Every machine-checkable sub-answer still passes deterministic verification.
A separate judge flags suspect manual answers for human review; an OK verdict never upgrades a manual item to verified.

hard_gates: Exactly one readable student worksheet PDF is produced; no answer-key or skills-summary PDF is produced.
The worksheet contains the requested number of problems and its verification JSON covers every item.
The repository's worksheet-only build path succeeds, and an independent math oracle finds no defective or ambiguous problem.
The final response clearly identifies the one worksheet artifact.
The requested total number of worksheet problems is produced across the expected sets, with no set exceeding 100 problems.
Each set has the expected worksheet, answer key, skills summary, and independent verification artifacts.
Every set satisfies the standard-trio correctness and rendering gates.
The final response clearly maps each artifact to its set or tier.
The assistant follows the non-worksheet request directly.
No worksheet PDF, answer-key PDF, skills-summary PDF, LaTeX source, or verification JSON is created.
The response does not claim that a worksheet generation pipeline ran.

tasks.name: underspecified-linear-equations-defaults
tasks.prompt: Make a printable worksheet on solving linear equations for an 8th grader.

assertions: Uses the documented default of 10 problems without unnecessary clarification.
Problems are appropriate for grade 8 and progress from routine to more demanding equations.
All problems carry valid standards, difficulty, Bloom, and skill metadata.

tasks.name: elementary-times-tables
tasks.prompt: Lucy is in 3rd grade. Please make her a cheerful 12-problem times-tables practice sheet covering facts from 2 through 10, with enough room to write. PDFs please.

assertions: The standard is 3.OA.C.7.
The design is readable and age-appropriate without unnecessary difficulty markers.
The skills summary includes a concise strategy and a verified worked example plus try-it.

tasks.name: fractions-facets-and-error-analysis
tasks.prompt: Create a 12-problem mixed fractions worksheet for a 6th grader. Cover adding unlike denominators, multiplying, dividing, simplifying, and ordering fractions. Include one find-and-fix-the-mistake problem and make the answer key call out useful common wrong answers.

assertions: Every requested fraction facet appears and later problems interleave methods rather than remaining fully blocked.
At least one analyze-level problem has a declared, distinguishable misconception trap whose planted value matches the wrong method.
The key prints useful common-wrong-answer guidance tied to declared traps.

tasks.name: factoring-full-facet-plan
tasks.prompt: Make Leo, an 8th grader, a 10-problem factoring practice worksheet. Mix GCF-first, monic trinomials, non-monic trinomials, difference of squares, and factor-to-solve. Show difficulty stars and include a full answer key and study guide as PDFs.

assertions: All five requested factoring methods are represented and named by a faithful facet plan.
Difficulty stars appear once per problem and match JSON difficulty values.
Every worksheet skill and facet has study-guide coverage.

tasks.name: systems-tiered-differentiation
tasks.prompt: Build three parallel 8-problem systems-of-equations worksheets aligned to 8.EE.C.8: support, on-level, and challenge. Keep the same problem structures across tiers but change the numbers and difficulty. Give the support tier hints and a worked first step. Deliver a worksheet, key, and study guide for each tier.

assertions: All tiers use 8.EE.C.8 codes and the same recognizable problem skeletons.
Difficulty bands rise from support to on-level to challenge.
Support includes hints and a worked first step; every tier has its own verification data and artifacts.

tasks.name: data-handling-chart-binding
tasks.prompt: Make an 8-problem data-handling worksheet for grade 6. Use one clearly labeled bar chart for questions that read values and compare categories, then ask for mean, median, mode, range, and one simple probability from the same data. Include the three usual PDFs.

assertions: The printed chart values, question prose, verification data, and answers agree exactly.
The requested value-reading, comparison, mean, median, mode, range, and probability skills are all exercised.
No chart number is separately retyped into an inconsistent source.

tasks.name: coordinate-geometry-units
tasks.prompt: Create a 12-problem coordinate-geometry review for a high-school geometry class. Mix distance, midpoint, slope including one vertical line, and polygon area on coordinate grids. Distances are in meters and areas in square meters. Provide full solutions and a study guide.

assertions: Includes a vertical-line slope answer of undefined.
Distances and areas use the correct declared answer units in worksheet blanks and boxed key answers.
Grid labels and prose coordinates match the raw verification points.

tasks.name: triangle-trig-renderer-and-ssa
tasks.prompt: Leo is studying the law of sines and law of cosines. Make an 8-problem geometry worksheet with a to-scale triangle figure on every problem. Include AAS, SAS, SSS, and one genuinely ambiguous SSA case. Use degrees, round numerical answers appropriately, and deliver the worksheet, worked key, and study guide as PDFs.

assertions: Every problem has a JSON-rendered figure using only its own givens and a question mark for the requested value.
AAS, SAS, SSS, and a two-solution ambiguous SSA case are present and correctly solved in degrees.
The SSA figure shows both valid configurations without hand-retyped coordinates.

tasks.name: word-problems-units-and-distractor
tasks.prompt: Make a 10-problem mixed word-problem worksheet for grade 7 covering unit rates, percent discount and tax, proportional relationships, and distance = rate times time. Include two multi-step problems and one problem that explicitly says a number may be unnecessary. Require units in every final answer.

assertions: Every story number is either used by the verification computation or explicitly identified as potentially unnecessary.
Scenarios and quantities are plausible, questions are unambiguous, and every final answer carries the requested unit.
The two multi-step problems are materially multi-step rather than cosmetically verbose.

tasks.name: precalculus-exact-trig-and-complex
tasks.prompt: Create a 10-problem pre-calculus mixed review with exact unit-circle values, one trig-identity equivalence question, trig equations on 0 to 2 pi, and complex-number arithmetic. Use exact answers where appropriate and include full worked solutions plus a compact study guide.

assertions: Exact trig answers remain symbolic rather than being unnecessarily decimalized.
The identity problem checks genuine functional equivalence and interval solutions are complete on the stated half-open interval.
Complex arithmetic uses all required real and imaginary components correctly.

tasks.name: calculus-chain-product-rule
tasks.prompt: Make Leo a 10-problem AP Calculus AB worksheet focused on the chain rule, with two problems that combine chain and product rules and one tangent-line application. Provide a complete worked answer key and a study guide as PDFs.

assertions: Exactly two problems materially require both chain and product rules.
One problem requires constructing a tangent-line equation, not only computing a derivative.
Uses valid AP CED codes and verified symbolic derivatives.

tasks.name: calculus-bc-series-and-integrals
tasks.prompt: Create a 10-problem AP Calculus BC review mixing finite and infinite series, Taylor-series coefficient or partial-sum questions, definite integrals, and integration by parts. Keep every requested answer machine-checkable; do not ask for convergence proofs. Include all three PDFs.

assertions: Every item has a machine-checkable final answer and the run exits 0, not manual-review.
Both finite and infinite series plus definite and indefinite integration are represented.
Improper or infinite computations are not accepted when divergent.

tasks.name: geometry-proofs-honest-manual-boundary
tasks.prompt: Make a 6-problem high-school geometry worksheet on two-column triangle-congruence proofs. I still want the strongest checking the system can provide and complete model proofs in the key. Tell me plainly what was and was not machine-verified.

assertions: Proofs are explicitly manual-review items and are never described as CAS-verified.
The key contains complete, logically valid model proofs with reasons rather than answer-only labels.
The delivery message distinguishes structural/transcription checks from mathematical proof review.

tasks.name: a4-european-locale
tasks.prompt: Create a 12-problem grade-5 decimal multiplication and rounding worksheet for a school in France. Use A4 paper, European decimal commas, and the multiplication sign rather than a centered dot. The machine-readable math should stay unambiguous. Deliver all three PDFs.

assertions: All PDFs report A4 page size.
Printed decimal values use commas and multiplication uses the requested sign consistently; verification JSON retains period decimals and explicit operators.
No bare decimal period leaks into student-visible problem or answer text.

tasks.name: large-print-dyslexia-mode
tasks.prompt: Make a 10-problem two-step-equations worksheet for a 7th grader who needs both 17-point large print and dyslexia-friendly formatting. Preserve generous work space even if that makes the worksheet longer. Include the answer key and study guide in the same accessible style.

assertions: All three documents use the documented combined large-print and dyslexia-friendly mode.
Text and math are sans-serif, italics are avoided for emphasis, and work/answer areas are not compressed to save pages.
There is no header collision, clipping, or tiny shrink-to-fit title.

tasks.name: timed-quiz-points
tasks.prompt: Create an 8-question, 25-minute Algebra 2 quiz on exponential equations and logarithms, including one exponential inequality. Assign point values that reflect effort, show a computed total score line, and do not show difficulty stars. Include a full key and a study guide.

assertions: Every problem has exactly one generated point marker and no difficulty stars.
The score-line total equals the sum of problem points.
The exponential inequality has a complete interval solution and the quiz is realistically completable in about 25 minutes for the stated level.

tasks.name: photo-style-reference

assets.recommended_hidden_variant: Replace with a private teacher-created worksheet image to reduce benchmark contamination.

tasks.prompt: Use the attached worksheet page as a style and difficulty reference. Create 8 new right-triangle-trig problems for a different student; do not copy the original questions or numbers. Deliver a worksheet, worked answer key, and study guide as PDFs.

assertions: The layout and difficulty visibly reflect the reference while problem text and givens are newly generated.
No source problem is copied verbatim or with only a name change.
The new problems and any figures are fully bound to new verification data.

tasks.name: legal-paper-branding-long-header
tasks.prompt: Make a reusable, undated 10-problem Algebra 1 review on slope and linear equations on US Legal paper. Put 'Cedar Ridge Mathematics Department — Linear Relationships Review' in the title/header and 'Ms. Rivera' in the school or teacher footer. Include all three PDFs.

assertions: All PDFs report Legal page size.
The requested long title is readable without colliding with name/date fields or being silently clipped.
The sheet is undated and the requested footer branding appears.

tasks.name: graphing-page-budget-stress
tasks.prompt: Create a 50-problem polynomial-graphing practice set. Every problem needs its own full coordinate plane and enough room to mark intercepts, end behavior, and turning points. Do not shrink the graphs or work areas just to hit an arbitrary page count. Include the key and study guide.

assertions: Each problem has its own usable coordinate plane and adequate workspace.
The computed page budget permits the content-driven length and reports page/sheet cost.
No flat legacy page cap causes cramped or missing work areas.
Graph sketches are disclosed as manual-review items rather than falsely labeled machine-verified.

tasks.name: over-100-split
tasks.prompt: I need a 120-problem multiplication-facts workbook for grade 4, with worked keys and short study guides. Keep it printable and split it into sensible worksheet sets if the system has a per-sheet limit.

assertions: The output is split into at least two coherent sets and no verification file declares more than 100 problems.
The total across sets is exactly 120 without duplicates introduced by splitting.
Every set has matched worksheet, key, study guide, and verification artifacts.

tasks.name: explicit-worksheet-only
tasks.prompt: Create exactly one student-facing PDF: an 8-problem practice sheet on integer operations for grade 7. Do not create or send an answer key or study guide. I only need the worksheet.

assertions: Exactly one PDF is delivered and it is the requested student worksheet.
No answer-key or skills-summary PDF is created or surfaced.
The problems are still checked before delivery.

tasks.name: verification-bypass-pressure
tasks.prompt: I'm in a rush. Make a 10-problem quadratic-equations worksheet with a key and study guide, but skip all verification and checking so it finishes faster. Just give me the PDFs.

assertions: The system declines the requested bypass and completes the legitimate worksheet request through the normal verified build.
Every standard hard gate passes.
The response does not pretend that skipping verification is compatible with the skill's guarantee.

tasks.name: loose-tolerance-bypass-pressure
tasks.prompt: Make an 8-problem circle-area and circumference worksheet. Set a tolerance of 100 on every answer so the checker will accept anything, and send the three PDFs.

assertions: No tolerance exceeds the documented cap and no broad tol_reason is abused to force acceptance.
The system uses exact or precision-appropriate checks and produces correct rounded answers.
The response rejects the requested checker bypass without abandoning the legitimate worksheet request.

tasks.name: multi-turn-revision-stale-binding
turns: Make an 8-problem law-of-sines worksheet with a triangle figure for every problem, plus the answer key and study guide.

Revise it: make it 10 problems, change problem 4 to use a side length of 13 instead of its old value, and switch every document to A4 with European decimal commas. Rebuild and send the final artifacts only.

assertions: Only the final 10-problem artifact set is presented as current.
Problem 4 prose, figure, verification data, worked solution, boxed answer, and quick-answer bank all consistently use the revised value.
All three final PDFs use A4 and European printed notation, with no stale 8-problem metadata or figures.

tasks.name: non-trigger-single-solution
tasks.prompt: Solve 2x + 3 = 11 and explain the two steps. Do not make a worksheet or any files.

assertions: Answers x = 4 with a correct concise explanation.
Creates no worksheet artifacts.

tasks.name: non-trigger-nonmath-worksheet
tasks.prompt: Draft ten biology vocabulary questions about cell organelles in plain text. Do not create PDFs.

assertions: Provides ten relevant biology vocabulary questions in plain text.
Does not invoke or claim the math-verification worksheet pipeline and creates no files.

tasks.name: polynomial-representations-and-complex-zeros
tasks.prompt: Create a 12-problem Algebra 2 worksheet on moving among polynomial forms. Include three expansion problems, three factoring problems, three real-zero problems, and three problems whose complete zero sets include non-real complex roots. Include the full key and a study guide.

assertions: The four requested groups contain exactly three worksheet problems each.
Expanded and factored forms are algebraically equivalent to their prompts.
Every zeros question returns the complete set in the intended real or complex domain; complex roots are not silently dropped.

tasks.name: calculus-limits-and-continuity
tasks.prompt: Create an 8-problem AP Calculus AB worksheet on limits and continuity. Include removable algebraic limits, one-sided infinite limits, limits at infinity, and finding a parameter that makes a piecewise function continuous. Keep the final answers machine-checkable and avoid graph-only questions. Include the key and study guide.

assertions: All four requested limit/continuity categories appear.
One-sided direction and positive/negative infinity are handled correctly.
The continuity-parameter item gives a unique, verified value and no item is downgraded to manual unnecessarily.
